increment_paragraph: **RULE32A-PILOT** (pluggable-cards seam B, phase P2, the last pilot of GATEWAY-RULE-API-PILOT-MIGRATIONS; [report](../../reports/rule32a-pilot/README.md)) decides what "off" means for a hold and moves gateway rule 32a onto the rule interface's token hold. Decision (plan §6 item 10, a card decision under the invariants): a hold is not switchable. A refusing off would let the logger's own row read its sibling's caller-frame declaration and be `Safe` again (widening); an off that holds more never widens but moves no frame member's row, only outside callers', so its ledger would be rule 32's filed under 32a. Registry row `32a` (`off = "not-switchable"`, the first hold and the first reserved reason key, `caller-frame-self-reliance`/`incomplete-obligation-coverage`) names the package `crates/gateway-rules/rule-32a-caller-frame-hold` (`CallerFrameHold: TokenHold` over its own `FrameHost` capability: held iff the call stays in one registered frame and the callee's declaration is in force), asked by `legacy_caller_frame_hold` in all three token pipelines through `consult`; the host keeps the member bodies, call positions and the held spelling. `QCORE_GATEWAY_RULES_OFF` naming `32a` is refused, and `gateway_rules::enabled` now answers `true` for a hold before reading the list (it answered `false` for every id under a refused list, which would have removed a hold). The rule API re-exports `ReasonCategory`. `caller_frame_hold.rs` is unchanged and green; new `rule32a_hold.rs` (refused lists, the hold on under the fallback and under accepted lists), gateway registry tests, package tests bound to the Lean table, Python registry tests. Lean `QCore.CallerFrameHoldSwitch` (13 audited theorems): the package's table, `holds_iff` with `withinFrame`, the fixed switch never removes the hold or widens, `a_refusing_off_would_widen`, `holding_more_changes_no_member_row`, `holding_more_moves_an_outside_row`. Rule 32a has no switch-measured ledger, by the decision. Identity: pending.

ledger.why: DISCHARGE (RULE32A-PILOT, 2026-10-31): the decision is recorded in the plan (docs/plans/pluggable-cards/README.md section 6 item 10, pointed to from section 3 B): a hold is not switchable. A refusing off widens (Lean a_refusing_off_would_widen: the logger's own row is Safe again); an off that holds more moves only outside callers' rows (holding_more_changes_no_member_row, holding_more_moves_an_outside_row), i.e. rule 32's reading, not 32a's. The switch with its tests: registry row 32a off = not-switchable; RulesOff::parse refuses any list naming 32a; gateway_rules::enabled answers true for a hold under every list, a refused one included (gateway unit test rule_32a_is_a_fixed_hold; integration test crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/rule32a_hold.rs re-running itself under QCORE_GATEWAY_RULES_OFF=32a, 35,32a and 33,34,35,36,37; Python test_gateway_registry; Lean QCore.CallerFrameHoldSwitch the_switch_never_removes_the_hold, the_switch_never_widens).

DISCHARGE (RULE32A-PILOT, 2026-10-31): every pilot landed as its own card with an identity run (35 and 37 on their own runs; 33, 34 and 36 through RULE36-PILOT's shared round-2 run; 32a in RULE32A-PILOT's run, report section 4) and every switchable pilot has its switch-measured ledger (contract/contributions/{35,37,33,34,36}/). Rule 32a migrated to crates/gateway-rules/rule-32a-caller-frame-hold (registry row 32a, known to known_rule) and has no switch-measured ledger by the GATEWAY-RULE-API-HOLD-OFF decision: a fixed hold has no switch, and the measurable quantity behind it is rule 32's (CONTRIBUTION-LEDGER-RULE-32-32A, amended). That clause is the one judgment in this retirement. Parity cost of the last pilot for plan decision 6: about 10 decision lines moved to a 90-line package module (127 with lib.rs); +1,046 -27 lines in the code commit in all (package with tests 340, host +95 -14, switch and its tests +94 -6, integration test 167, Lean 231); about 16 minutes from the brief to the code commit; the rest is the identity measurement (report section 7).

ledger.text: RULE32A-PILOT (2026-10-31): rule 32a is a fixed hold (plan section 6 item 10, GATEWAY-RULE-API-HOLD-OFF retired), so --rules-off 32a is refused by design and 32a has no switch-measured ledger; the 7 recorded rows are callers outside the frame reading the caller-frame declarations, i.e. rule 32's contribution (Lean QCore.CallerFrameHoldSwitch.holding_more_moves_an_outside_row). Amended DISCHARGE: a card registers rule 32 with a refusing switch over the outside callers' reading of the caller-frame declarations (off: the declaration is not read, which never widens), then quirin-audit measure on the live profiles --rules-off 32 writes rule 32's ledgers with contribution_ledgers.py write, consistency passes, and the report compares the measured rows and premises with the recorded 7.
